name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Kiros's large fundraising advantage over Peterson
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
Open seat after DeGette lost renomination
model.rationale: The D+29 district fundamentals make this overwhelmingly Democratic, and Melat Kiros's roughly $1.1 million raised plus outside support dwarfs Christy Peterson's ~$2,000 in receipts. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at the baseline margin.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or a scandal involving the Democratic nominee could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver-based CO-01 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+29. Longtime incumbent Diana DeGette is not on the ballot after losing renomination, but the seat remains safely in Democratic hands. Democrat Melat Kiros has raised over $1 million and drawn substantial outside spending, while Republican Christy Peterson has raised only about $2,000.

Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's win odds around 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-to-high twenties.
